subject.title: Bug: 180s compaction timeout is a single wall clock over the whole chunk pipeline with no partial-progress reuse, so a legitimately-long compaction fails identically every turn

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the linked multi-pass/progress-tracking design for compaction recovery, or constrain the fix to committing the last usable summary on timeout without persisted cross-attempt checkpoints?
rationale: Both paths address the observed blocked-session failure, but they differ in session-state durability, recovery semantics, and compatibility scope; source inspection alone cannot choose the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Review the multi-pass proposal
options.body: Use the linked implementation as the canonical path if it proves safe progress reuse and bounded session-state behavior.

options.title: Narrow to last-summary recovery
options.body: Keep recovery in the existing compaction boundary by committing a usable completed summary when a later quality or timeout step fails.

options.title: Retain timeout-only configuration
options.body: Keep the current timeout behavior and document configuration as the sole remedy, accepting that overflow recovery can remain blocked.

recommendation.title: Review the multi-pass proposal
recommendation.body: Use the linked implementation as the canonical path if it proves safe progress reuse and bounded session-state behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is connected to the active progress-tracking implementation candidate referenced by the issue.
